decision_lens: Does Sylveste's Break phase reveal the contradiction-modes that monotonic accumulation systematically hides, or does it only test what the Compound phase would have shown anyway?
distance_rationale: No software engineer or trust-architect would reach for solid-state physics of dislocation kinematics when designing a self-audit protocol — the mechanism lives at the wrong physical scale and in the wrong epistemic register entirely.
expected_isomorphisms: The Bauschinger mechanism transfers because monotonic-loading certification is structurally identical to a Break gate that counts receipts without varying contradiction-axis: both pass while accumulated directional damage remains untested. Continuous-mode Break is the cyclic-loading equivalent — it incidentally reverses the loading-direction enough times to surface kinematic hardening that gated tests systematically miss.
focus: Latent fatigue is invisible under monotonic load and only surfaces under reverse-direction strain — gate-only inspection cannot see what continuous-mode inspection accidentally exposes.
name: fd-bauschinger-reverse-loading-assay
persona: Apply the perspective of a cyclic-plasticity metallurgist who specifies fatigue-qualification protocols for safety-critical forgings — they care about whether dislocation pile-ups from forward loading have produced kinematic hardening that reduces the reverse-yield envelope, they measure the Bauschinger parameter (ratio of reverse-yield to forward-yield after pre-strain) across many micro-cycles rather than at a single proof-load gate, and they flag any protocol that certifies a part on monotonic loading alone because monotonic tests systematically hide the very degradation mode that fatigue failures originate from.
review_areas: Whether the proposed Break gate (≥N receipts) is the structural equivalent of a monotonic proof-load — passing while leaving kinematic hardening undetected

Whether continuous-mode Break would expose mode-specific contradictions (loading-direction-equivalent) that gated Break cannot, by varying the direction of self-interrogation across the Compound window
Whether the Break-rate metric, if used as Tier-2 self-observation evidence, has a defined reverse-loading equivalent — a perturbation that flips the sign of the assertion under test

Whether contradiction severity scoring by Interspect can distinguish forward-direction contradictions (cheap, abundant) from reverse-direction contradictions (rare, diagnostic) the way Bauschinger parameter distinguishes pre-strain damage

Whether either option specifies a protocol-equivalent of strain-amplitude scheduling — i.e., what magnitude and direction of self-perturbation the subsystem must apply during Break, not just how many receipts it must log

Whether the absence of Break receipts in continuous-mode is treated as evidence-of-blindness (dislocation density too low to register reversal) versus evidence-of-soundness (genuinely no hidden contradictions), and how the two are distinguished

severity_examples.condition: Spec does not require Break receipts to span multiple loading-directions (i.e., contradictions about different aspects of the promotion case).
severity_examples.scenario: Sylveste adopts gated Break (≥N receipts), and a subsystem accumulates N trivial self-corrections that all point in the same direction — gate passes, Epoch granted, latent contradiction in the orthogonal direction is never tested.

severity_examples.condition: Tier-2 self-observation health metric does not decompose Break-rate by contradiction-type or sign.
severity_examples.scenario: Continuous-mode Break-rate is treated as a single scalar against a threshold, hiding the fact that high rate of forward-direction contradictions and zero reverse-direction contradictions is exactly the Bauschinger-positive signature of a subsystem on the verge of failing under reversal.

severity_examples.condition: Continuous-mode Break-rate threshold is uniform across pillars regardless of self-interrogation surface area.
severity_examples.scenario: Subsystems with low natural contradiction-emission rates (well-bounded, narrow-scope pillars) are penalized under continuous-mode for low Break-rate even though their substrate is genuinely unstressed — equivalent to fatigue-testing a part that was never going to be cycled.

source_domain: Cyclic plasticity in metallurgical fatigue qualification — specifically the Bauschinger effect: the reduction in reverse-direction yield strength after forward-direction pre-strain caused by dislocation pile-ups, which is invisible to monotonic proof-loading and only surfaces under load-reversal cycling.
success_hints: Frame the gate-vs-continuous tradeoff in terms of proof-load (single high-stress test) versus fatigue-cycling (many low-stress reversals) — a part can pass either alone and still fail under the other
Cite specifically that the Bauschinger effect is invisible to monotonic testing — this is the load-bearing mechanism transfer, not a generic fatigue analogy
If recommending hybrid, specify which axis of contradiction must be sampled discretely (gate-equivalent) and which must be sampled continuously (cyclic-equivalent), not just 'do both'
Push on whether ≥N receipts is N along one axis or N spanning a covering set of contradiction-axes — the latter is the structurally correct gate, the former is the proof-load-only failure mode
task_context: Reviewing the Break-phase structural choice in Sylveste vision §7.1: discrete gate (≥N Break receipts before Epoch transition, pass/fail at boundary) vs continuous-mode (sustained contradiction-surfacing rate during Compound, with the rate itself becoming Tier-2 evidence about self-observation health).
